  project from a clean clone of the checkout, so it takes copier's 3-way path
  on every run, and its make-driving test drops make's inherited variables.
- **Four refactor tests no longer write into the checkout.** The execute-mode
  tests of `tests/integration/test_practice_refactor.py` wrote their
  checkpoints under the checkout's `wiki/.runtime`, where a later run could
  resume a crashed one's snapshot; each now checkpoints under its own
  `tmp_path`.
- **`tests/unit/scripts/test_audit_project.py` no longer flakes on a network
  scratch root.** Its no-write snapshot compared a directory's modification
  time, which moved between two snapshots with no write on a network mount; it
  now compares a file's time and the sorted listing.

### Security

- **The config loader's refusals never echo a URL's user part.** When
  `scripts/config_loader.py` refuses a string that holds an `@` anywhere
  (`https://user:token@host`, `https:/user:token@host`, a scheme-less
  `user:token@host`), its line shows `<hidden: it holds an @>` in place of the
  value, whatever the key, because the part before the `@` may be a
  credential. A URL urllib cannot split, such as `https://[::1`, is a refusal
  with exit 14, not a traceback. A list member or object entry name the line
  names is hidden the same way when it holds an `@`, and a member that is a
  list or an object is hidden when any string inside it, a key name included,
  holds one at any depth. A key written twice and an adapter name a refusal
  names are hidden the same way, and so is such text in the refusals
  `scripts/child_env.py` raises at a child's start and in the `make_targets`
  policy refusal `scripts/run_make_target.py` passes on, through the loader's
  one rule, `shown`. So does every finding checks A to Z of
  `scripts/check_structure.py` build from configured text, error or warning,
  for a value, a member, a key name or a path segment, while a harmless member
  beside it still shows, and so does the tree's own text: an ADR's file name
  and directory show beside a hidden number space or prefix, and a campaign
  or slice number beside a hidden id template. An `adr.project_dir` or
  `adr.template_dir` spelled with a `.` segment, such as `./docs/adr`, is
  refused as one with `..` is: check_Y matched a space by its spelling, so it
  judged every ADR there out of place and printed the directory raw. So does every refusal
  `scripts/launch.py` builds from the `launcher` block, a list member by member
  through the loader's `quoted` and `listed`, and every refusal the evals
  config, the live run and `scripts/run_evals.py` build from the `evals` block,
  a line of paths item by item through `joined`, and every line
  `scripts/exit_code_table.py` writes naming the `doc_drift` guide or gate
  target, and every refusal and red-record line `scripts/gate_evidence.py`
  builds from `evidence.dir` or `evidence.schema`, and every message
  `scripts/shell_gate.py`, `scripts/scan_secrets.py` and
  `scripts/install_scanner.py` build from the `shell` and `secrets.scanner`
  blocks, a run-date value `scripts/run_date.py` refuses, and the credential
  variable names `models/openai_compatible.py` refuses an `api_key_env` over,
  a scratch root `tests/isolation_guard.py` refuses or passes over, and an
  extra `scripts/check_venv.py` finds undeclared, and a protected-path rule key
  or reason `scripts/apply_refactor.py` refuses an edit over, an answer-set
  name, answer key or scratch root `scripts/canary.py` refuses, the baseline
  path `scripts/expiring_tier.py` refuses, and a variable name a
  `child_env.prefixes` entry admits from the environment in
  `scripts/child_env.py`'s credential refusal. The loader names a file it
  cannot read the same way, and none of these refusals chains an error whose
  message holds the text it hides, so a traceback of one that escapes, as from
  a gate test, hides it too. A configured name, prefix,
  label, scheme, host or answer-set name that ends in a newline is refused:
  its pattern's `$` matched before the newline, so it passed and printed as
  written.
  Before, a `secrets.scanner.release_url` given a token was refused with the
  token in the message.
- **A confidential document reaches no reader the project serves.** The
  corpus recorded each node's visibility, but nothing in `src/backend/showcase`
  read it. So a `confidential` document's text came back from
  `/api/wiki/node`, `/api/search` and `/llms-full.txt`, and went into the
  static export `make site-static` publishes. The practice refactor agent, the
  index enforcer's summary fill and the doc reviewer could each put a hidden
  document's text in a model prompt. `scripts/query_corpus.py` printed any
  node, and a served node's links still named a hidden one by id.
  One allowlist, config/project.json `corpus.served_visibilities` (`public` and
  `internal` by default), now decides for every reader: the showcase API, both
  llms files, the static export, the wiki navigator, the practice refactor
  agent, `scripts/query_corpus.py`, the index enforcer and the doc reviewer.
  `scripts/config_loader.py` `is_served` is the one copy of the decision; four
  copies of the filter are gone, a class fix. `cut_hidden` drops hidden ids
  from a served node's links, children and parent. A node at any other level
  is absent rather than redacted, and a request for it is answered as an
  unknown node. A document that states no level is built as `internal` and
  served by default; only a corpus row with no `visibility` field is treated
  as hidden. The doc reviewer reports a finding it withholds, with the reason,
  and withholds every finding when the corpus or config cannot be read. A
  level outside the vocabulary, the corpus's `unreadable-readme` marker
  included, is refused as a config fault (exit 14) naming the member, so
  nothing is served. A generated project gets the key with its config.
  `scripts/query_corpus.py` and the agents that retrieve through it (the
  wiki navigator, the MCP Q&A server, the practice refactor and the doc
  reviewer's style rules), the doc reviewer's findings, and the showcase's
  node detail and markdown body also ask the level a node's file states on
  disk now, through `scripts/corpus_level.py`, the reader
  `scripts/jobs/build_corpus.py` uses. `config_loader.is_served_now` serves
  the node only when the stricter of that level and the corpus's is served,
  so those readers neither send nor serve a document reclassified after the
  corpus was built, nor name it in a served node's links. A file whose level
  cannot be read now is not served either. The showcase's doc tree, search,
  counts and neighbour refs, the `/llms.txt` index, the headings in
  `/llms-full.txt` and the static `tree.json` still list a reclassified
  node's title and summary until the corpus is rebuilt; CONVENTIONS §1 lists
  each reader on each side. CONVENTIONS §1 also names the residual risk: a
  served document's own link text can name a hidden document's path, which a
  default id is derived from. A corpus is read only with the files of the
  checkout that keeps it at `wiki/corpus.json`: `scripts/query_corpus.py`,
  the wiki navigator, the MCP Q&A server, the doc reviewer and the practice
  refactor each take a root or a corpus and derive the other
  (`scripts/corpus_level.py` `checkout`). They refuse a root and a corpus
  given together, an empty root, which would read their own checkout, a
  corpus path that is not some directory's `wiki/corpus.json`, and a corpus
  path that does not exist, so a mistyped
  corpus is not answered from an empty context. So the MCP Q&A server answers another project's corpus
  against that project's files. `query_corpus.py` refuses a `--root` that
  does not exist, and the wiki navigator then raises before a model call.
  `query_corpus.py` writes to stderr how many nodes it withheld, and where a
  checkout with no corpus would keep one. Each of the three agents makes a
  relative path absolute from the caller's directory first. The doc
  reviewer fails its run when `query_corpus.py` refuses its style-rule
  retrieval, rather than asking a model for edits with no rules, and
  `scripts/doc_review.py` then exits 2 naming the root, not with a traceback.
  An execute run fails the same way when the retrieval finds no rule node at
  all; a dry run, which calls no model, shows the empty rules section in its
  preview.
  `query_corpus.py` refuses a corpus it cannot read with exit 2.
  (KEEL-VIS-2)
- **The astro app's audited dependencies move past their advisories.**
  `npm audit` in `src/frontend/astro` reported 28 findings (2 critical, 17
  high); each fixable package moved in its own commit within its declared
  range, never with `npm audit fix --force`. `dompurify`, which sanitises
  rendered markdown in the visitor's browser, rises to `^3.4.17` and
  `mermaid` to `^11.16.1`; devalue, http-cache-semantics, smol-toml, svgo,
  js-yaml, nanoid, source-map-js, postcss, the lint plugin's
  postcss-selector-parser 7, fast-uri, brace-expansion, both
  vite copies and `@astrojs/check` move in the lockfile only. A generated
  project ships the same two files. Left open, because each fix is a breaking
  major: `astro` itself (critical from 7.2.8, every astro advisory only from
  7.3.2) with the sharp and
  esbuild it pins, the lint plugin's `braces` chain (no fixed `braces`
  exists; the way out is eslint-plugin-astro 2 on ESLint 10), the
  postcss-selector-parser 6 that `@tailwindcss/typography` pins (moderate),
  and the katex 0.16 that mermaid 11 pins (low). `src/frontend/react-vite`
  audits clean.
- **An audit finding left open has one place to say why, and an end date.**
  `make fe-audit` (`[read]`, `scripts/audit_dependencies.py`) runs
  `npm audit --json` in each frontend app and judges it against
  config/project.json `dependency_audit.accepted`: rows of advisory id,
  package, reason and `review_by` day per app. It fails a critical or high
  finding no row covers (`dependency_audit.fail_at`), a row past its day, a
  row dated more than `dependency_audit.max_review_days` (90) days out, so an
  acceptance is renewed rather than parked, and a row whose advisory the audit
  no longer reports; a moderate or low finding
  is listed, not failed. It refuses a report it cannot trust instead of
  passing it: counts that disagree with the entries, or no audited
  dependency while `package.json` declares one (a workspaces root's
  `workspaces` included, a peer marked optional not), which is how an empty
  lockfile audits. A failed run shows npm's own cause with every URL path
  hidden, a scheme-less host's path included, and every userinfo up to its
  last `@` hidden, a bare `user@` before a host or a bracketed IPv6 host
  included. A URL keeps its scheme only when npm reaches that scheme (`http`,
  `https`, `socks`, `socks4`, `socks4a`, `socks5`, `socks5h`, `git`,
  `git+http`, `git+https`, `git+ssh`, `git+file`, `ssh` and `file`); after any
  other `://` the userinfo and path are hidden as well. A secret word's value
  is hidden after `=` or `:` whatever it is, to the end of the line or the
  next `name=`, so cause text after it on that line goes too; a `<hidden>`
  another rule wrote, or a scheme name, at the value's start is kept and the
  rest is still hidden. `Bearer` and `Basic` are keys as a secret word is, so
  the words after the value the scheme rule hid are judged too, and a
  `realm=` right after either is kept as written, so npm's `Unable to
  authenticate, need: Basic realm="..."` keeps the registry's realm. In prose the
  clause after the secret word opens after a space or any mark (`password,`,
  `password's`, `[token]:`, `password/`) and goes on past a `<hidden>`
  another rule wrote, and each of its words is hidden
  unless the closed vocabulary `scripts/audit_dependencies_data.py` lists
  holds it, it is three marks or fewer, or it starts with a URL; the URL word
  ends where the URL does, at a comma or semicolon after its host and port
  too, so text glued before it or after that mark is a word of its own, and
  its host is kept only when it is a named host (a dotted name, an IPv4 or a
  bracketed IPv6 address) and is `<hidden>` otherwise. Each cause word cites the npm or Node.js
  message that holds it, so `password required`, `token is self-signed` and
  npm's `401 Unauthorized - POST <url>` read as written. The clause ends at
  `.`, `!` or `?` only before a capital or the line's end, and never at a
  period after a single letter (`e.g.`). The costs: a password that is a
  vocabulary word, a capitalised value after a real sentence end, a secret of
  three marks or fewer, a value written as a URL's named host after a secret
  word or as the realm after `Bearer` or `Basic`, and a value joined by `-`,
  `.`, `_` or nothing to a key word (`auth`, `token`, `password`, `passwd`,
  `secret`, `key`, `credential`, `cookie`, `Bearer`, `Basic` or
  `Authorization`), which reads as part of the key's name, are shown; a cause
  word the vocabulary lacks is
  hidden, a single-label host such as `localhost` after a secret word is
  hidden, and a secret word inside a longer word (`monkey`, `Unauthorized`)
  hides the words after it.
  The advice reads the raw text and is unchanged. The registry's host is kept when it is a DNS name,
  a single valid label such as `nexus3`, or a bracketed IPv6 address whose
  zone id, with only a leading `%25` decoded, is no longer than an interface
  name (a longer zone is hidden and the host kept); any other host that mixes
  letters and digits, such as a token passed as the registry or as one of
  its labels, is hidden whole. A label is kept unless its parts that are no
  word, taken together, form a run of 20 or more mixed characters, so a token
  behind or between word parts is hidden; a run that is one word and then a number is a
  name's shape and is kept, so both
  `my-domain-111122223333.d.codeartifact...` and
  `acme2024-111122223333.d.codeartifact...` stay readable. The line is cut to
  `dependency_audit.max_shown_chars` (500) characters so a registry's long
  body can neither flood the line nor stall the redaction, and a quoted
  value the cut splits is hidden whole. A key followed by a letter or digit
  opens no clause, so a line of `token` repeated is read once rather than
  once per key, and a clause word is read at most 300 characters at a time,
  so that pattern's runs are bounded as every other's are. The run says to
  check the registry URL when npm reports `Invalid URL`, the `.npmrc`
  credentials when the registry refused the login, and reachability when it
  could not be reached.
  It runs npm with every
  dependency type included, so an
  `.npmrc` `omit=` cannot narrow it, and writes nothing in the tree; npm
  writes its own per-user log and cache. It is not a `make verify` goal, because the
  registry's answer changes day to day. Keel's first row, also shipped to a
  generated astro project, accepts the postcss-selector-parser 6 finding
  until 2027-01-21: its only fix is a breaking downgrade of
  `@tailwindcss/typography`, and it parses the project's own stylesheets.
  `docs/guides/deterministic-checks.md` section 16 says how to accept a risk.

## [0.3.0] — 2026-10-15

- **ADR-K-0016 and ADR-K-0017 are accepted.** A release tags locally, runs
  the full gate, and pushes only on green; `make verify` writes its evidence
  record through `scripts/gate_evidence.py`. ADR-K-0017 names the goals the
  recipe runs today, `trace` and `eval` included.

### Added
- **Imports flow up a configured layer order, and the tree is held to three
  more rules.** config/project.json `import_layers.order` lists the layers
  bottom to top, and `tests/integration/test_import_layers_gate.py` fails an
  import into a higher layer, a Python file no layer holds and a layer entry
  that places no file (ADR-K-0021, proposed). check_D also fails
  `from pkg import _sub` of a private submodule from outside `pkg/`.
  `tests/integration/test_exit_gate.py` fails a `fail` or `finish` call
  outside the entry block of a module another project module imports, unless
  `import_layers.may_end_the_process` names it with a reason.
  `tests/integration/test_swallowed_error_gate.py` fails a bare `except:` or a
  broad handler that only drops the error unless its suppression gives a
  reason, and `tests/integration/test_change_comment_gate.py` fails a comment
  that opens with a `change_comments.phrases` phrase. The four tests share one
  reader of the tree, `tests/source_tree.py`. **Action required:** each rule
  fails a project's own code from the first `make test` after
  `copier update`, with no warning period. The ruled warn-then-fail tier is not built,
  and no date for it is set: 2027-01-31 is a proposed default the maintainer
  has not ruled on, and no config key carries it until the tier reads one.
- **A shipped gate test and a shared scripts module each need a features
  row.** `tests/integration/test_reference_drift.py` derives every
  `tests/integration/test_*_gate.py` and every `scripts/` module another module
  outside `tests/` imports, from the import graph, and fails one with no row in
  `docs/reference/features.md`, which gains the `Gate tests` and `Shared script
  modules` sections. The CONVENTIONS §2 note about importable `scripts/`
  modules states no count and cites that derivation, and the same test fails
  it if it states a count again. The derivation reads your project's tree,
  not keel's file list: a project whose own code adds a
  `tests/integration/test_*_gate.py`, or a `scripts/` module another of its
  modules imports, goes red on update until the page has its row.
- **"Nothing judged" has its own exit code, 13.** `ExitCode.NOTHING_JUDGED`
  means a run found no item to judge, so it cannot answer yes; it is
  non-zero and outside the launcher's reserved and farm statuses.
  `scripts/long_scripts.py` exits 13, not 1, when no recorded run carries a
  duration, and `make exit-codes` gives the member its row.
- **`scripts/launch.py` decides where a long script runs, and says why in one
  line.** It reads three facts: the host kind, the script length and the farm.
  A host is `own` only when a pattern in the git-ignored file
  config/project.json `launcher.own_hosts_file` names matches it; with no such
  file every host is `shared` (`config/own-hosts.example.json` is the
  placeholder twin). A script is long when `launcher.long_scripts` lists it or
  its last recorded run took more than `launcher.long_after_seconds` (`600`),
  and unknown, which counts as long, until a recorded success proves it short.
  The farm is the `launcher.farm.adapters` entry `launcher.farm.adapter`
  names; it ships as `none`, with a Slurm argv adapter as one option. A farm
  job, an own host or a short script runs here; a long or unknown script on a
  shared host runs here at `os.nice(launcher.limited.niceness)` when there is
  no farm or `launcher.local_only` names it, and is submitted otherwise. The
  command starts from `build_child_env`, so a farm job receives the allowlist,
  the `models.credential_env` names of the model adapter the launch key's
  `launcher.credentials` entry names, and the adapter's rendered env, and a
  launch whose environment holds an unlisted credential name is
  refused before anything runs. The command's status passes through. A farm
  that does not start it within `launcher.farm.wait_seconds` hands it back to
  a spare host, and otherwise the launch ends with `ExitCode.NO_CAPACITY` (12)
  and runs nothing. Each run is written whole to the git-ignored
  `launcher.durations_file`: the outcome, whole seconds, the status and where
  it ran. A full farm on a busy host, and a launch killed while its command
  runs, never replace a measured run over `launcher.long_after_seconds`, so
  `make long-scripts` still proposes it. `--dry-run` prints the decision line and runs nothing.
- **`make long-scripts` proposes the scripts to list as long.**
  `scripts/long_scripts.py` reads the durations file and prints a `propose:`
  line for each launch key whose last run took longer than
  `launcher.long_after_seconds` and that `launcher.long_scripts` does not
  list. It edits nothing, and a file with no measured run fails, because
  judging nothing is not "none is long"; it is in neither `make check-all`
  nor `make verify` for that reason. `docs/adr/keel/K-0020-shared-compute-launcher.md` is the
  accepted decision; it is defence in depth for shared compute, not a
  scheduler.
- **The `openai-compatible` adapter sends its credential only to a host
  config lists.** config/project.json `models.allowed_hosts` maps an adapter
  to `host` or `host:port` entries, matched exactly on the host and port of
  `base_url` in the one form `scripts/child_env.py` `canonical_host_entry`
  defines; an entry with no port matches only the scheme's default port, and
  nothing matches by suffix, prefix or wildcard. It ships as
  `{"openai-compatible": []}`, so every host, the adapter's default one
  included, is refused until a project lists it. The check runs at
  construction, before any request is built and before the credential
  variable is read; the `ValueError` names the key and the entry to add, and
  `make eval-live` refuses with exit 2. check_X refuses an entry in any other
  form, a duplicate, and an adapter not in `models.available`. The adapter
  also refuses every redirect: urllib re-sent a POST answered 301, 302 or 303
  as a GET with the Authorization header to the host the `Location` named.
  An `http` base_url is refused unless its host is a loopback address
  literal (127.0.0.0/8 or `::1`; the name `localhost` is refused), so the
  credential never crosses a network in clear text. Defence in depth, not a
  sandbox;
  `docs/adr/keel/K-0018-model-endpoint-host-allowlist.md` is the accepted
  decision. **Action required:** a project that calls `openai-compatible`
  adds its endpoint's host to the list after `copier update`, as the upgrade
  guide says.
- **One date per gate run.** A `make verify` that crossed midnight turned red
  on every document touched that day, because
  `tests/integration/test_doc_freshness.py` and `make check-docs` each read
  the clock when they started. `scripts/gate_evidence.py` now reads the clock
  once, before the first goal, and hands that date to every goal in the
  variable config/project.json `evidence.run_date.env` names
  (`KEEL_GATE_RUN_DATE`), which `child_env.names` lists.
  `scripts/jobs/review_docs.py` `resolve_today` reads it after `--today` and
  `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` and before the clock, through the new
  `scripts/run_date.py`. A value found in the variable is checked on every
  read: a calendar date written `YYYY-MM-DD`, no later than the clock and at
  most `evidence.run_date.max_age_days` (`1`) days before it. Anything else is
  an exit 2 that names the variable, never a fall back to the clock. The
  variable can therefore move a check's today back by the bound and never
  forward. `docs/adr/keel/K-0019-one-date-per-gate-run.md` is the accepted
  decision. A project that keeps its own `child_env.names` must add the name;
  the upgrade guide says how. check_X reads the same block, so a variable
  `child_env.names` does not list is a `make check` error before any run, and
  `make check-docs`, `make restamp-docs` and `make audit-project` answer a
  fault in the block with the config edit that clears it, not with
  `--today`.
  The test suite's own commits are dated by the run too:
  `tests/hermetic_git.py` `git_env_vars` adds `GIT_AUTHOR_DATE` and
  `GIT_COMMITTER_DATE` from `scripts/run_date.py` `git_dates` when the
  variable is set. Without them a tree the suite committed after midnight was
  dated a day past the stamps the run wrote, and a run from 23:18 to 01:08
  failed three goals on committed-stale documents (measured).
- **One exit helper and a closed list of exit codes.** `scripts/exit_codes.py`
  holds `ExitCode` (`SUCCESS` 0, `FAILURE` 1, `USAGE` 2, `RED_RECORD` 10,
  `BACKEND_ABSENT` 11, `NO_CAPACITY` 12, `INTERRUPTED` 130) and the one
  `sys.exit` in the tree.
  One number carries one fact: `scripts/gate_evidence.py` exits `RED_RECORD`
  when every goal passed and the record is red, and `scripts/run_evals.py`
  exits `BACKEND_ABSENT` when the live backend did not answer. 10, 11 and 12
  are values no shell, argparse, make, pytest, `sysexits.h` or signal status
  uses, so `make: Error 10` cannot be read as pytest's internal error (3).
  `tests/integration/test_exit_codes_cli.py` starts each script as a child
  process and reads the status and the three message parts. A script's entry line
  is `finish(main())`; `main` returns a member, a failure through
  `report(member, what failed, on which input, what to do next)`, which writes
  one stderr line and refuses a blank part, and a wrapped tool's status
  through `passthrough(...)`. `tests/integration/test_exit_gate.py` fails an
  exit written anywhere else, an entry block that returns anything but
  members, and a missing or blank-literal message part. The exit-code table in
  `docs/guides/limits-and-troubleshooting.md` is generated by
  `scripts/exit_code_table.py` (`make exit-codes`, `[tree]`), and
  `make check-exit-codes` (`[local]`, a prerequisite of `make check-all`)
  fails a stale one. Every script a release shipped keeps its numeric codes;
  no script exits 3. The last stderr
  line of a failure changed to the three-part form, so a caller that matched
  the old text must match the new. A project script that calls `sys.exit` is
  red after an update until it ends through the helper.
- **Requirement traceability, judged in `make verify`.** A `kind: spec`
  document under config/project.json `traceability.specs_root` (`docs/specs`)
  defines a requirement with a heading that opens with an id, and a numbered
  criterion with a `- AC-<n>: <text>` line beneath it. An id is
  `<prefix><digits>` or `<prefix><digits>#AC-<n>`, under a prefix
  `traceability.id_prefixes` lists (shipped: `REQ-`, four digits); an unlisted
  prefix is refused and there is no fallback. A test names what it is evidence
  for with `@pytest.mark.req("REQ-0001#AC-1")`. `make trace` (`[local]`, a
  `make verify` goal and a CI step) runs `scripts/trace_requirements.py`,
  which gives every criterion, and every requirement that has none, one
  verdict: `covered`, `gap` (a reason under `traceability.gaps`) or
  `uncovered`. A bare requirement id never covers a requirement that has
  numbered criteria. It writes the canonical matrix to
  `.evidence/traceability/matrix.json` under
  `config/traceability/matrix.schema.json` and exits 0, 1 for a finding or 2
  when it could not judge. A marker that names no defined unit, a marker on
  nothing pytest collects, a gap for a covered unit and a project with no
  requirement and no `traceability.no_requirements` reason are findings.
  `tests/integration/test_requirement_traceability.py` judges the same tree
  in the suite, and fails when a child `pytest --collect-only` disagrees with
  the reader about which collected test carries which id. An id or a
  criterion written in a form the grammar does not read, and a document under
  the specs root that defines a requirement without `kind: spec`, are refused
  (exit 2), never skipped. It shows that a test names a requirement, not that the test
  proves it. `docs/specs/example-feature.md` and the markers in
  `tests/unit/backend/test_example_feature.py` are the worked example; a
  project that removed that test and takes this update must remove the spec
  or name its requirements.
- **Evals that judge actual responses, replayed in `make verify`.** `evals/` is
  now a harness, not a placeholder. A suite is one `evals/datasets/<suite>.jsonl`
  file, one canonical case per line, held to
  `config/evals/eval-case.schema.json`. Each case names a doer (`prompt`, or
  the `triage` agent's real `triage` function), a deterministic scorer
  (`exact`, `contains`, `regex`, `json_fields`) and a recorded response with its hash and the hash of
  the prompt it answered. `make eval` (`[local]`, a `make verify` goal and a CI
  step) runs each doer against a backend that replays the recording. It fails a
  case whose prompt has changed as `stale-recording`, and a suite below config/project.json
  `evals.threshold` (`1.0`), compared as exact fractions. It writes a canonical
  report to `.evidence/evals/replay.json` under
  `config/evals/eval-report.schema.json`. `make eval-live` (`[read,cost]`) sends
  the same cases to `evals.live.model` under `evals.live.max_calls`, which
  defaults to `0` and is checked before any backend is built. It writes
  candidates for a person to promote and never edits the dataset. Refused (exit
  2), failed (1) and absent (11, `BACKEND_ABSENT`) stay distinct, and zero
  cases is refused.
  The `triage` function in `agents/triage` now also accepts an injected
  `backend=`.
- **The `openai-compatible` adapter refuses a credential variable config does
  not declare.** Its `api_key_env` argument picks which environment variable
  is sent to `base_url` as the bearer token, and `evals.live.model_options`
  forwards config to it, so config could name any variable and any host. The
  adapter now accepts only a name listed in config/project.json
  `models.credential_env.openai-compatible` (shipped: `OPENAI_API_KEY`) and
  only an http or https `base_url` with a host and no user part, query or
  fragment, written in URL characters only (no space, control character,
  backslash or non-ASCII character), and it requests the URL rebuilt from the
  parts it checked; either refusal is a `ValueError` at construction and exit 2 from
  `make eval-live`, before any request. It describes an unexpected response
  body by its keys instead of quoting it, reports a reply that is not JSON
  without a copy of it, names an endpoint in an error by
  scheme, host and port and never by its path, and a live eval report replaces the value of each
  declared credential variable with `<hidden>` in its case details.
  `scripts/run_evals.py` refuses a report path that resolves through a
  symlink before it writes or deletes anything.
- **Upgrading: the `openai-compatible` credential is declared in config.**
  `copier update` brings `models.credential_env.openai-compatible`, listing
  `OPENAI_API_KEY`, into `config/project.json`
  (`tests/integration/test_copier_audit.py`). A project that passes another
  variable as `api_key_env` adds that name to the list; without the entry, or
  without the name, every construction of the adapter is refused.
- **End-to-end scenarios over a real socket, and a gate that every endpoint
  has one.** The REST scenarios in `tests/e2e/` now drive the real app under
  uvicorn on a loopback port the OS picks (`tests/live_server.py`, the
  `rest_server` fixture), and the MCP scenarios speak JSON-RPC to the real
  servers over their stdio (`mcp_session`); no scenario uses an in-process
  client. The new gate `tests/integration/test_e2e_coverage.py`, run by
  `make test`, derives every endpoint an enabled transport serves from the code
  (the REST app's OpenAPI document, each MCP server's `tools/list`, each
  `.proto` service method) and fails when one is named by no
  `@pytest.mark.endpoint` scenario and not exempt with a reason. A marker or
  exemption naming no endpoint, a redundant or reasonless exemption, an
  unreadable marker, a marker on no collected test, and a served route the
  OpenAPI document cannot list are each red; the last is an allowlist over a
  walk of the routes the app loads, so a route form nobody anticipated is red
  too. The server is ready within `e2e.server.ready_timeout_s`, each request
  and each child is bounded, and the server's process group is killed even
  when a scenario fails or SIGTERM or SIGHUP ends the test run. The settings live in the new config/project.json `e2e`
  block; a generated project with `grpc` ships its one method exempt, because
  no gate builds the gRPC stubs yet. The gate checks naming, not what a
  scenario asserts.
- **Frontend unit tests and a browser journey in the gate.** Each shipped
  frontend app (`astro`, `react-vite`) now carries a unit runner, the npm
  script `test:unit` (Vitest over `src/**/*.test.ts`, and `.tsx` in
  react-vite), and a browser journey, the npm script `test:e2e` (Playwright
  builds the app, serves it with its own preview server and drives it in
  headless chromium over `e2e/*.spec.ts`). `make test-fe-unit`,
  `make test-fe-e2e` and `make test-fe` run them, and `make verify` gains a
  fifth goal, `test-fe`, recorded in `.evidence/verify.json` with its result and
  `tests: null`. A suite with zero tests fails, a focused (`.only`) test fails
  in either suite, a red test fails the gate, and with `node_modules`
  installed a missing browser is red. With a frontend app, a host without
  `npm` or an app without `node_modules` exits 2 before any app runs, naming
  the app and `make fe-install`, so the gate never passes over tests that
  never ran; a project with no frontend app stays silent. `make fe-browsers`
  downloads the journey's browser through each app's npm script
  `test:e2e:browsers`, CI runs `make fe-browsers` and then `make test-fe`
  after `make eval`, and the READMEs' Quickstart runs both install targets
  before `make verify` when a frontend ships.
  The journey's server reads the new config/project.json keys
  `layers.frontend.journey.host`, `port`, `server_timeout_ms` and
  `browser_executable`, and refuses a busy port rather than reuse whatever
  answers there; an IPv6 host is written bare and bracketed in the URL.
  `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` joins config/project.json `child_env.names`, so
  a relocated browser cache reaches the journey under `make verify` as it does
  under `make test-fe`. `tests/integration/test_gate_scope.py` fails an app
  missing either script, either config, a test file, the shared runner pin, a
  journey key or the refusal of a focused test. No browser is downloaded under the gate. A generated project
  with a frontend receives both suites and the keys; a `none` project receives
  neither.
- **A typed evidence record for every gate run.** `make verify` now runs its
  goals through `scripts/gate_evidence.py` and writes `.evidence/verify.json`
  (config/project.json `evidence.dir`, an ignored directory). The record names
  the commit, whether the tree was dirty and a digest of what git lists, each
  goal's result and exit code, pytest's own junit counts and every
  `scripts/check_structure.py` finding. It follows `config/evidence/gate-record.schema.json`,
  the only owner of `schema_version`, and holds no clock, host, user or absolute
  path, so a rerun of the same tree writes the same bytes. A red goal, zero
  tests, a missing test report, a tree that changed during the run or a writer
  that crashed leaves a red record, never the previous green one; the driver
  writes a red placeholder before the first goal. The gate is stricter in
  four ways: zero tests (an all-skipped suite counts as zero), a missing junit
  report, a tree changed during the run, and a junit report counting a failed
  or errored test whose goal exited 0 anyway now fail it (under `make -i` the
  exit stays 0, as `-i` asks, and the record is red). `KEEL_REQUIRED_EXTRAS`
  joins config/project.json `child_env.names`, so a declared surface still
  fails rather than skips under the driver. The record keeps no history, is
  unsigned, and under `make -j` the goals still run in sequence.
  `docs/adr/keel/K-0017-gate-evidence-record.md` records the decision.
- **The feature catalogue and the settings reference.** `docs/reference/settings.md`
  lists every setting keel reads: each key path of `config/project.json` and
  `config/practices.json`, each copier question, make variable, environment
  variable and command-line flag, with its type, default, valid values,
  reader, effect, what it is not for, and which projects receive it. The new
  `config/project.json` key `doc_drift.settings_reference` names the page, and
  `tests/integration/test_reference_drift.py` derives every expected set from
  the code and fails on a setting with no row, a row the code no longer reads,
  or a literal default that differs from the code's. A generated project gets
  the page and the test; the copier-question checks skip there with a stated
  reason. A project whose own code adds a JSON key, an environment variable, a
  make variable or a flag goes red on update until the page has its row.
  `docs/reference/features.md` lists every feature keel ships, one row each,
  with what it does and why, how to run it, the settings it reads, its limits,
  its guide and which projects receive it. The new `config/project.json` key
  `doc_drift.features_reference` names the page, and the same test derives
  every check letter, make target and its effect label, checker script,
  copier job, agent, MCP server, model and runtime adapter, workflow and skill
  from the tree, fails on one with no row, and fails on a row with an empty
  Limits cell. `tests/unit/backend/test_showcase.py` holds the showcase's
  curated features equal to the page's pillar table. A project whose own code
  adds a make target, an agent or a checker goes red on update until the page
  has its row.

### Fixed
- **`passthrough` no longer passes a script's own status off as a wrapped
  tool's.** `tests/integration/test_exit_gate.py`, through
  `scripts/exit_code_table.py`, fails `finish(passthrough(main()))`,
  `passthrough` over `main`'s result directly or through a name, over an int
  literal or a member, and over a function of the same script whose every
  return is one of those, also under a sign (`-1`), combined with `or` or
  arithmetic, or through a builtin such as `int(...)`. A `main` that returned
  integers wrapped that way passed the gate before.
- **`make -i` no longer lets a `[write]` target past `WRITE_GUARD`.** Under
  `-i`, `--ignore-errors`, `MAKEFLAGS=i` or a bare `.IGNORE:`, make ignored the
  guard's `exit 1` and ran the write under CI or a gate run, exit 0. The guard
  now opens with a make `$(error)` that fires when the first word of
  `MAKEFLAGS` holds `i`, which stops make whatever its flags, attended runs
  included. check_W requires that clause in the guard's definition and
  refuses any `.IGNORE` rule, because `.IGNORE: <target>` ignores errors
  without touching `MAKEFLAGS`. `tests/integration/test_write_guard.py` runs
  each flag against a real make.
- **A git command that ran and failed is no longer read as "no git".**
  `scripts/git_tree.py` raised `NoGitError` for every git failure, and
  `scripts/run_evals.py` and `scripts/gate_evidence.py` then wrote without
  the ignore check, as they do where there is no repository. It now raises
  `NoGitError` only when git is not installed or no `.git` entry exists where
  git would search, and `GitFailedError`, with git's exit status and stderr,
  for anything else. `scripts/gate_evidence.py`, `scripts/run_evals.py`,
  `scripts/trace_requirements.py` and `scripts/run_make_target.py` refuse on
  it with exit 2 and write nothing. A corrupt repository, or one git refuses
  as unsafe, now stops `make verify` instead of passing unchecked.
- **The evidence writer refuses a path reached through a symlink.**
  `scripts/gate_evidence.py` checks the record, its temporary file and every
  goal's junit report with `scripts/git_tree.py` `through_symlink` before its
  first write or delete, and exits 2 naming config/project.json
  `evidence.dir`. A symlinked `.evidence`, a symlinked parent or a symlinked
  record file could carry a write, or the delete of a stale report, outside
  the project.
- **A symlinked `.venv` is ignored like a real one.** `.gitignore` named
  `.venv/`, `venv/`, `node_modules/` and the other tool directories with a
  trailing slash, which git matches only against a directory; a `.venv`
  symlink to a shared environment was committed by `git add -A`, and as an
  untracked file it blocked `copier update`. Every plain directory name now
  carries no slash, and `tests/integration/test_ignore_patterns.py` plants a
  symlink for each name in both `.gitignore` and its template twin and asks
  git whether it is ignored.
